target_customer: Real estate agents and teams who pay per agent per month to have inbound leads qualified by text
problem: Agents lose leads because they cannot reply within minutes and follow up persistently; Riley concierges texted leads to qualify them.
business_model: B2B subscription per agent per month with human concierges (Inman reported 25 dollars per agent per month, up to 75 for teams of four)
product_category: Real estate lead qualification by SMS

founders.name: Helson Taveras
founders.background_notes: Listed as the only founder on the YC page, with no bio.

founders.name: Daniel Ahmadizadeh
founders.background_notes: Named as CEO in a geekestateblog interview title and in Product Hunt comments (search results). Not on the YC page.

exit.reason: Inman reported the company was closing and returning remaining cash to investors; the stated reason in the headline snippet was not landing a scalable, high quality solution users loved in real estate.

competitors.name: Magic and GoButler
competitors.what: Text based assistant and concierge services named in the same Inman article about automated assistants in real estate

technical_complexity.rationale: Human concierges sent texts through an SMS platform; the engineering was messaging and CRM integration, with the hard part being operations and quality.

defensibility.rationale: Texting leads with trained staff is copyable and the Inman snippets show no data or integration lock in.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Real estate CRMs such as Zurple later offered mass texting (undated vendor blog), but the sources opened do not show an incumbent copying Riley before it closed in 2019.

market_need_then: Inman 2016 described agents needing minute-level responses to leads; Riley grew revenue 17x during YC per a Medium post by its investor (search result), but no spend figure was verified.

branding.name_origin: CEO Daniel Ahmadizadeh said in a Product Hunt comment that the product was named after Steph Curry's daughter Riley Curry (search result summary; a casual comment, not an official statement).
branding.domain_note: Product Hunt and Wellfound listings use getrileynow, suggesting the exact domain was not available (inferred from slugs, unverified).

identity.mascot_or_character: Human sounding assistant persona (inferred from concierge texting), not documented
identity.voice_and_tone: Friendly personal text conversations by concierges per Inman 2016

brand_strength.rationale: A friendly human name fit a texting concierge, but it was generic, shared by many products, and no press on the brand itself was found.

outcome_analysis: Riley used human concierges to text real estate leads, raised a 3.1 million seed in April 2017 after YC Winter 2017, and told investors in March 2019 it was closing and returning remaining cash. The Inman headline snippet cites not finding a scalable, high quality solution users loved, which points to scaling a human heavy service rather than demand. Competition and any pivots after 2017 were not documented in sources opened.
notes: Inman pages could not be fetched (domain safety check rate limited), so details come from search snippets; the shutdown reason and investor list should be confirmed. The seed is stated by Inman and TechCrunch; the investor list came from a database listing and not from the cited article. Company website field is empty. The competitor Magic and GoButler is known only from an article title dated 2015-08. YC tagline says Mailchimp for SMS but the product was concierge lead qualification; founding year not found.
